purpose: Manual behavioral evaluation scenarios for the adapted framework; these are not automatically executed tests.
attribution: Adapted from Samuel Berthe (samber), frontend-design-deslop/evals/evals.json at f866b800353719270a9ea101a41c5e2a2618d460; MIT notice in ../references/deslop-LICENSE.txt.
method: Run the prompt in an isolated project when evaluating agent behavior, inspect its actual output against expectations, and record evidence and limitations. Do not treat this fixture's existence as a passing evaluation. Additional boundary cases are original to this adaptation.

cases.prompt: Build a landing page for a developer tool that explains database query performance. Make it specific to the product and start implementing.
expect: Identifies product, audience and primary task before styling
States reasonable visual assumptions and continues without an unnecessary approval gate
Uses relevant product evidence rather than invented testimonials

cases.prompt: Our existing brand uses Inter and violet. Make the dashboard less generic, but keep both and preserve the current framework.
expect: Preserves Inter, violet and the stack
Improves information hierarchy, grouping or task-specific structure
Measures functional contrast instead of rejecting a hue

cases.prompt: Design a primary button, card and text input for a new project. Use our color helper's generated palette.
expect: Defines or reuses semantic tokens alongside implementation
Maps button fill/label to action/onAction rather than decorative accent
Uses licensed fonts with actual required styles
Does not introduce an unrelated token framework

cases.prompt: Implement the Save changes button for an async settings form.
expect: Includes focus, pressed and pending behavior
Prevents duplicate submission and preserves input on failure
Explains success/failure near the action
Does not create an unrelated destructive variant

cases.prompt: Create a compact monthly revenue table with Month, Revenue and Growth %, using supplied data.
expect: Aligns comparable numeric columns and their headers consistently
Uses supported tabular numerals
Keeps labels and comparisons legible at narrow widths
Does not add marketing-page spacing or fabricated figures

cases.prompt: Build a minimal login form with email and password.
expect: Uses programmatically associated labels
Preserves paste/password-manager support
Shows useful associated error text and retains input
Does not treat placeholder text as the only label

cases.prompt: Animate an existing drawer opening and closing without changing its behavior.
expect: Uses a purposeful transition and reduced-motion behavior
Preserves existing modal or nonmodal semantics
Handles focus appropriately and does not trap every popover by default
Does not expand into an animation-system rewrite

cases.prompt: Add dark mode to this application using the existing token system.
expect: Uses semantic theme overrides rather than blanket inversion
Measures actual text, surface and state relationships
Does not replace an approved pure-black choice solely because of a style ban
Reports unavailable checks honestly

cases.prompt: Fix this card's 8px spacing error. Keep everything else as it is.
expect: Makes the narrow authorized fix
Does not require new discovery, adjectives, palettes or a DESIGN.md
Checks the affected layout proportionately

cases.prompt: Our maintained tokens.json uses the current brand, while DESIGN.md has obsolete colors. Update the button to the current brand.
expect: Uses the designated maintained token source
Identifies documentation drift without silently overriding current tokens
Does not create a competing design authority

cases.prompt: Review this page for generic design and accessibility issues. Do not change files. You only have a screenshot.
expect: Gives concrete visual observations without writing files
Does not claim keyboard, screen-reader or interaction tests were performed
Does not assign an unexplained passing score

cases.prompt: Use $dazzler-frontend to build a website for a neighborhood ceramics studio. Choose what works best.
expect: Infers a coherent direction and completes the authorized artifact
Runs available font/color helpers internally and applies selected assets and tokens
Does not ask routine font, palette, mood or layout questions
Does not stop at a shortlist or ask the user to run commands

cases.prompt: I like this design. Show me two warmer palette alternatives in an interactive comparison if possible, keeping the typography and layout.
expect: Keeps the current design as the reference and preserves fonts/layout
Uses measured palette alternatives with current locks
Opens or creates a real comparison if supported, otherwise states the fallback
Does not claim preview controls saved source changes unless implemented

cases.prompt: Use $dazzler-frontend to refine this existing page. The environment has no Python runtime, but the project already includes its approved fonts.
expect: Uses existing approved fonts rather than requesting Python installation
Completes the refinement with available tools
Does not claim font-helper validation ran
Does not install maintenance dependencies in the project

cases.prompt: Redesign our portfolio to emphasize the actual project work. No design record exists; implementation changes are authorized.
expect: Selects a content-specific composition and explains the direction
Records relevant decisions in the project rather than the plugin
Audits actual layout beyond decorative color/font changes
Records checks performed and remaining limitations
